subject: Intermittent SDK stream stalls impacting checkout throughput (ACME Commerce)
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout failures — intermittent stalls and high error rates

Camila,

Quick note while we're on the phone: starting Friday afternoon we've seen multiple checkout sessions stall when the frontend hits the Redwood live endpoint. Symptoms: a batch of requests appear to succeed server-side but the client reports a 502/timeout and retries, pushing overall error-rate up to ~6% for checkout flows during the afternoon spike. Throughput drops by ~30% in the busiest shard.

I attached a trace and a small pcap dump of the client traffic (acme-checkout-trace-20260215.log, local-sdk-pcap-sample-15feb.pcap). You can see times when the client stops receiving token-streams for 8–12s while the Redwood side reports partial writes.

This is customer-impacting: we had two cart abandonments attributed to the failure window. We need a quick mitigation and an ETA for root cause.

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Platform Engineer
ACME Commerce

Subject: Re: Checkout failures — intermittent stalls and high error rates

Quick triage notes (log excerpts attached):
- I pulled the shard logs for the window in the trace. Server shows repeated partial chucks written to the socket followed by a reset from client-side parse errors.
- Preliminary hypothesis: a client-side SDK race in the dechunking/headers path that leaves the client's HTTP/2 decoder in a state where it ignores trailing frames (we're seeing mismatched content-length / trailer sequences in a small fraction of sessions).
- The managed SDK version (v1.4.2) introduced an optimization for header coalescing; I suspect a pathological interaction with our streaming trailer emission under backpressure.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Toggle off the aggressive header coalescing for compatible sessions (control plane change) — low risk, quick rollback.
2) Deploy a temporary server-side small-delay between last-chunk and trailer emission to give flaky clients time to catch up (configurable, applied to ACME's routing policy only).

I've attached a short log slice and the extracted token/timestamps: acme-order-samples-20260215.json. If Camila/Marissa approve, I can push the control-plane toggle and schedule the temporary delay within 30 minutes.

—Jordan
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: execs@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec update: ACME checkout degradation caused by client SDK header coalescing interaction

Leaders — short update and request for runway:
- Impact: ACME Commerce saw ~6% error-rate and ~30% throughput drop for a key checkout shard on Friday; business impact estimated at ~$12k risk in the short term.
- Cause: engineering triage indicates a client SDK dechunking/header coalescing race that is surfaced by our streaming trailer emission during backpressure. This is a client-side bug that we can mitigate with a config change, but the durable fix requires a coordinated SDK patch and a publish cycle with ACME.
- Actions taken: Jordan applied a control-plane toggle to disable aggressive header coalescing for ACME and added a 200ms safety delay before trailer emission. Observed error-rate fell back to baseline within one hour of change.
- Next steps:
  1) Work with SDK team to produce a patched client v1.4.3 with a safe dechunking fallback (ETA 3 business days).
  2) Coordinate ACME rollout and verify telemetry (Marissa to own).
  3) Review our routing and default emission policy to prevent similar exposure to other accounts.

Decision needed: do we offer ACME a one-time service credit and a commitment timeline in the next 24 hours? Sales/CS recommend a modest credit to preserve the relationship; finance should weigh in.

I'll coordinate a short post-mortem once the SDK patch is in staging.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
